name: Serial repetition
summary: One motif or one frame, repeated with small changes in a set of works, so that the viewer reads the change and not the object.
how: Fix the motif, the format and the viewpoint; change one variable only, such as the hour, the colour or the stripe width.
Make at least 5 works in the set and show them in one row at one height.
Keep the spacing between works equal to a fixed unit, such as 10 cm or one panel width.
Remove the hand: use a mechanical edge, a stencil or a plain lens.

origin.note: Claude Monet shows a group of Haystacks canvases, each of one motif in a different light.

adoptions.via: Frank Stella starts his Black Paintings, in which equal stripes repeat the shape of the canvas.
Bernd and Hilla Becher begin their typologies of water towers, blast furnaces and houses on one fixed frame.
Andy Warhol repeats one soup can or one face in a grid of identical canvases.

sources.title: Bernd and Hilla Becher, Typologien industrieller Bauten (1963)
